subject: Urgent: Novara AI - spike in errors & latency, cross-region mitigation
thread_summary: Customer Novara reported a sudden regional spike in 5xx errors and increased 95thpct latency for the us-east-2 AZ. Internal team coordinated an exec bridge, proposed temporary cross-region steering to us-west-2, enabled cache/quantization fallbacks, and agreed an immediate mitigation plus a short credit ask while deeper postmortem and routing fixes are implemented.
messages:
From: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@novara.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: eng@novara.ai
Date: 2028-05-30 08:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Production - sustained errors and latency spike (us-east-2)

Hi Jonas,

We started seeing a big uptick in 5xx responses and long tail latencies beginning ~08:30 EDT (us-east-2). Error rate jumped from ~0.5% to ~7% and 95th pct latency climbed from ~420ms to 820-1200ms on our production prefix. We've attached a small sample of requests and pings. This is impacting our checkout flow; revenue is being affected.

Attached: novara-error-samples-20280530.jsonl, ping-traces-novara-05-30.tar.gz

Can you confirm whether this is a routing/capacity issue on your side or a model degradation? We need an ETA and temporary mitigation.

- Elena
Elena Cruz
Platform Lead, Novara AI
elena.cruz@novara.ai

Elena — thanks for the quick heads up and the samples. Creating an exec bridge now and pulling in SRE + CS.

Immediate plan (T-10):
- Opened bridge (joining details in Jira SUP-3210).
- Ops: investigate node-level saturations, memory/IO errors; Hannah, can you confirm whether eastus2 is reporting AZ-level throttling?
- If capacity is constrained, we'll initiate short-term cross-region steer to us-west-2 for 30% of traffic for the most latency-sensitive prefixes.
- As a fallback we can route customer requests to a quantized/reserved pool with slightly lower throughput but lower error rates.

Elena, we recommend preparing for a brief maintenance window (15m) if we need to drain and shift traffic — we'll keep you posted.

Date: 2028-05-30 08:57:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Production - sustained errors and latency spike (us-east-2)

On Tue, May 30, 2028 at 08:52 -0400 Jonas Weber wrote:
> Elena — thanks for the quick heads up and the samples. Creating an exec bridge now and pulling in SRE + CS.

Joining bridge now. Initial telemetry shows elevated queue depth on several GPUS in us-east-2-az-b and increased retry amplification at the router layer. No obvious kernel OOM yet but some sockets are transiently timing out which increases client-visible errors.

Immediate actions I'm running:
1) Spin a temporary dedicated pool (dedicated-usw2-temp-01) and warm model variant redwood-v2-medium-q4_0 that is quantized to reduce memory pressure.
2) Enable prefix (KV) cache for Novara's top 3 prefixes (they provided prefix list) to cut repeated token compute.
3) If queue depth doesn't decrease in 10m, we'll start the cross-region steer at 25% and ramp to 50% over 15 minutes.

I've opened SUP-3210 and added logs + initial traces: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3210

--
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@novara.ai>
Date: 2028-05-30 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Production - sustained errors and latency spike (us-east-2)

Quick note from customer-ops POV:
- Activate the fallback model variant (quantized) only for the problematic prefixes; do not apply account-wide to avoid quality regressions.
- Prepare a short customer credit ask (~50% of one hour of tokens impacted) to appease their leadership while we complete the postmortem. I'll draft language for approval. Vanessa, can you own comms + legal consent for steering?
- Capture a replay bundle for postmortem (attachments: included) so applied rate-limits and routing decisions are reproducible.

Also: consider temporarily increasing circuit-breaker threshold for Novara's route to reduce client-side retries while we shift traffic — that should lower amplified load.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@novara.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, eng@novara.ai
Date: 2028-05-30 09:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Production - sustained errors and latency spike (us-east-2)

Elena — quick status and agreed next steps from the bridge (summary for your execs):
- What happened: transient resource pressure in us-east-2 AZ (likely node-level IO saturation) caused queue amplification at the router layer and a spike in 5xxs and tail latency for Novara prefixes.
- Immediate mitigation applied (09:02 EDT): warmed dedicated quantized pool in us-west-2 and enabled prefix cache; began a controlled cross-region steer of 30% traffic for the top two prefixes. Observed error rate drop from 7% -> 1.4% and 95th pct latency from ~1.1s -> ~480ms for steered requests.
- Next 60min: continue ramp to 50% if stability holds; collect replay bundle and full traces; SRE will keep route circuit-breaker adjustments in place to avoid retry amplification.
- Compensation: Rishi will coordinate a short credit (proposed 50% of impacted window) and Vanessa will draft customer comms.

We will follow up with a postmortem within 48 hours and a remediation plan (routing hardening + improved autoscale thresholds). Meeting scheduled: 09:55 EDT bridge with Novara eng and Redwoods SRE + CS.

If you need anything right now, text me at +1 (415) 555-0134.

Thanks,
Jonas
